record_notes.DCP-LETT-1855: April 21, supplied 1856, nine retained blocks, complete footnotes and bibliography read; all three actual drawings viewed. The vertical-column puzzle is connected to prior Madeira discussion, not a located incoming letter. Darwin rejects uplift as sufficient explanation, proposes tentative viscous sliding and asks Hopkins/Forbes rather than reporting their approval. Three sketches show stepped lava, convex radial columns, and longitudinal flow with labelled transverse AA planes. No scale or quantitative angle measurement appears in the images. The 12-degree case is hypothetical in prose; thin versus thick beds and uncertainty about recollected figures remain. April 13–16 discussion and later 1858/1864 publication are distinct events.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1862: May 1–2, 1856, fifteen retained blocks, full annotations, all seventeen notes and bibliography read. May 1 text was expressly not posted that day; May 2 addition precedes sending. Earlier shell list is missing, and corrected nomenclature/Helix rufescens question mark do not reconstruct it. Woodward/Prentice beetle carrying Ancylus and Curtis spider eggs on Dytiscus are relayed reports, not Lyell or Darwin direct observations of those cases. Nanina name list has raw diag/ramme fragments and no restored table layout. J.E. Gray is the reported classifier, not Asa. Heer lending is future while Lyell still uses the paper; later August reading is not May access. P6 expressly urges a small species-theory publication; May 2 P14 retains Lyell specific-centre hypothesis. Undated Darwin annotations are separate from letter prose and do not fix receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1866: May 3, supplied 1856, seven retained blocks, all notes and bibliography read. Thanks long letter and explicitly confirms corrections to the retained shell list, responds to extraordinary transport reports and publication suggestion. Lava question resumes the separate April 21 problem; no answer from Lyell is preserved in May 1–2. P3 priority dilemma remains undecided, meeting proposed for Thursday May 8 at 9–10 rather than proved completed. P5 reports three plants from enclosed tree-root earth and 29 from pond mud; it does not report 29 plants germinating directly from a duck foot. Duck mud comparison is a demonstration to Hooker. P6 asks publishing venue, still hypothetical. Later May 14 journal start not backdated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1902: June 16 with supplied month/year, seven retained blocks, all notes and bibliography read. Cathartic objection to Forbes/Hooker/Wollaston/Woodward land extensions within living species duration, not endorsement of their conjectures. Quoted Woodward message remains missing; June 4 Woodward note does not uniquely supply this wording. P6 future loans of Webb, Heer and Maury not physical receipt. P7 Dont answer this is historical letter content, not a research instruction or evidence that Lyell could not answer. The following dated Lyell reply directly challenges the omissions in this criticism, with editorial relationship confirmation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1910: June 25, supplied 1856, seven retained blocks, all notes and bibliography read. Five-part geological argument replies to June 17; explicit before I got your letter versus now I must strike my colours records changed judgment about subsidence. Ramsay discussion is an additional oral input, with possible June 18 meeting not certain date. Copied letter corrected/completed by Darwin; original draft distinct. P3 Geographical is an uncorrected copyist reading where draft geological differs; preserve sent-copy wording and variant provenance. Hooker reading is requested conditionally, not accomplished dispatch/receipt. Darwin does not claim accidental transport already explains every case. Later Origin discussion is future, and species essay wording does not establish a published contemporary book.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1917: July 5, supplied 1856, seven retained blocks, all eight notes and bibliography read. Darwin acknowledges long Lyell answer, presses for verdict and answers volcanic subsidence/elevation arguments in P1–4. The surviving July 1 journal extract supports this section; its expressly unsent July 2 postscript is not a prompt. P5 permission to credit Lyell and proposed wording refers a missing part of the incoming letter: exclude it from an apparently source-complete pair based only on 1915A. Lyell dedication notebook quotation is separate modern apparatus, its June 29 date unverified and use as sent reply uncertain. Salutation, date, valediction and postscript are Darwin hand; main copy corrected by Darwin. Notions qualified throughout; apparent published-at-your-suggestion language concerns the proposed essay, not proof of publication. Later 1874 retained geological view remains future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1633: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Sunday within January 21–February 11, 1855 XML range; calendar candidates are January 21/28 or February 4/11, without one established day. Lyell letter forwarded from Down and now received; exact arrival unknown. Concedes serious gap: parallel foliation/cleavage was assumed distinct from bedding where that cannot be proved. Recalled earlier curve idea and tuff crystallisation case remain author claims. Actual P4 diagram shows quartz nodules and feldspar crystals in parallel layers, with no quantitative scale. Sorby paper not yet obtained. Conditional P.S. distinguishes metamorphosed clay-slate cleavage from other rocks stratification, not a settled universal resolution. Later published consensus not activated here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1672: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. April 23, 1855 incoming Lyell letter advocates Barrande foreign membership and endorses Dana. Distinguishes published merit from unpublished discoveries Lyell personally saw; thirty gastropod genera/150 species and 150 bivalves are Lyell reported evidence, with claim about Forbes polarity qualified nearly overturned. Proposed Cambrian terminology and French support are current opinion, not later uncontested history. No preceding Darwin letter survives to pair this reverse response. No automatic receipt on composition/council day. Independently located June 10 Darwin-to-Huxley 1697 explicitly encloses this old Lyell note in the same Barrande/Dana campaign, establishing a conservative known-by witness then. Later election failure and Dana 1884 election remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1679: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. May 8 with supplied 1855 year. Gives earlier published boulder reference, calls proportional ice-dressing argument new, and discusses viscosity/momentum manuscript appended to Ramsay paper. Wants to recover manuscript and perhaps publish it; August publication is future. Hopkins support recalled from earlier meeting, and Geological Society criticism refers to Lyell telling him, not necessarily a surviving letter. Does not answer April 23 Barrande/Dana source 1672; topics and identified inputs differ. Missing glacial enquiry and oral exchanges cannot be replaced by nearby catalogue record.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1772: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 4 with supplied 1855 year. Returns two Bachman pamphlets with evaluative criticism showing some reading, but exact pamphlet identities remain probable in summary. This does not imply reading Nott/Gliddon book, which apparatus dates to December. Pigeon pairs already alive, external observation underway, skeletonising planned; plant varieties and hybrids begun. Invitation remains prospective. P6 says he has just seen Lubbock and learned that New Zealand Flora was sent with Wollaston work; no blanket inference of Lyell receipt or reading. Later November 28 scientific journal remains future. No surviving incoming pamphlet cover or Lyell prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1905: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Lyell June 17, 1856 copy, ten blocks and complete apparatus. Challenges continental-area reasoning through Sharpe’s proposed glacial submergence, elapsed geological time and Darwin’s coral subsidence. Lyell qualifies post-Eocene geographical change rather than licensing all arbitrary land bridges. Haughton’s eleven-mile sounding is doubted, not established fact. New Zealand earthquake/tree age is analogy; Madeira/Porto Santo biological contrast remains question. Chatham/Raoul identification has editorial uncertainty. Darwin’s explicitly June 18 Hooker postscript acknowledges this side of the argument; known-by June 18, no exact receipt hour or final-copy wording guarantee.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1915A: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Lyell contemporary journal extract headed July 1, 1856, fifteen blocks, full notes/bibliography and all three actual figures read. Original sent letter missing; copy/extract is not proof of full dispatch extent. Volcanic elevation versus broad ocean subsidence debated with qualified mechanism, not a settled universal law. Source 12,000-foot sounding conflicts with apparatus 1,200; preserve discrepancy. P9 genuine MathML means one-half million years, not 12 million. First journal diagram is reportedly dated June 1 against July 1 heading, an unresolved layer. Drawings show hypothetical sea levels/volcano/deformed layers, littoral flanking beds and Grand Canary overlap; no measured scale. July 2 postscript in footnote 8 is expressly NOT sent to Darwin and cannot be incoming memory. 1919 P2 acknowledges main Lyell answer by July 5, while extent of copy/diagrams received remains limited.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1904: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. June 17–18, supplied 1856, eight blocks and full apparatus. Main text answers a missing Hooker note received June 17, weighing Huxley/Falconer/Cuvier and qualified morphological inference, with Wollaston book already read and separate missing Wollaston remark. Woodward continental-island report prompted June 16 letter to Lyell, but precise Woodward source is not fixed merely by similar subject. P7 explicitly dated 18th establishes Lyell June 17 letter known by June 18, not by June 17. P8 second postscript asks North-West American plant question and should retain its section/date context. Unidentified hand corrected ludged to lugged; no authorial correction silently inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1919: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Evening July 5, supplied 1856, all thirteen blocks, notes and bibliography. P1 develops Tristan/Antarctic-continent question from morning letter. P2 acknowledges Lyell long reply, P3 requests forwarding of Darwin’s letter, which is not yet established as done. P4–10 directly answer 1911: Flora/Laburnum translation and follow-up, Entada establishment, Aristolochia/Viscum and stigma readiness, parthenogenesis, Aldrovanda with remembered Candolle parallel, and Ray Society policy based on own Cirripedia experience. P11 £20 is pledge, not February 1857 recorded payment. P13 asks for intermediate-variety examples after Wollaston; other subject and missing prior cases. Editorial summary belongs to morning 1918. Receipt of Hooker note some days ago is relative, not an exact date. Lyell source is a journal extract of missing original, so known-by acknowledgement does not prove every retained diagram or unsent postscript was received.

visual_readings.visual_observation: P2 schematic sloping lava streams with step-like vertical divisions and parallel internal lines, labelled Lava Streams. It illustrates hypothetical movement; no quantitative scale or measured angle.
P3 convex semicircular lava section with radiating divisions and curved concentric bands. It illustrates the remembered narrow convex stream, not a measured section at a located site.

P8 elongated flow outline with longitudinal interior lines and oblique transverse lines labelled A at both edges. AA denotes hypothetical division planes guiding adjacent columns; no scale or recovered Forbes plate is established.

Viewed long horizontal banded sketch with small rounded nodules labelled nodules of quartz in upper layer, and elongate patches plus short block-like marks labelled crystals of Feldspar in lower layers. It illustrates P4 claimed tuff-to-crystal sequence; it supplies no scale or separately dated observation.

Two schematic panels: A/B/C terrain with F volcano, B–D and G relative sea levels and deep K–L baseline; lower H mound, p/q marine surfaces, curved m/n/o beneath m-prime/o-prime. No measured scale; illustrates regional subsidence and local volcanic uplift.
H is a low central swell with q at left and p at right, stippled marine beds at the flanks above baselines; this is the hypothetical littoral-deposit comparison, not quantitative data.
Grand Canary labelled section: inclined marine beds overlap older subaerial rocks, rising terrain to the right; no numerical dimensions. Supports relative stratigraphic geometry only.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
